look_here_first: Start with color and leaf shape. Leavenworth's eryngo is an annual that turns dramatically purple in the flowering canopy; its upper leaves are broad, deeply palmately divided, and sharply spiny. The flowering heads are elongated and topped by a conspicuous crown of spiny bracts.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: upper leaves broad and palmately divided into spiny lobes

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: conspicuous terminal crown/coma of spiny bracts

lookalikes.differences: Eryngium yuccifolium is a perennial with long yucca-like linear leaves and pale greenish-white globose heads, lacking the purple palmately divided canopy.
